requests.description: Run the repository-required make verify on the Ubuntu lab server; report build, race-test and vet results, actual toolchain, and any failures. This does not establish PostgreSQL parity or a complete product/security assessment.

Uriah explicitly authorizes installing Mossward on this existing Linux lab host, which currently has no Mossward installation. Build and verify this exact pinned product revision, then follow docs/LINUX_LAB_ACCEPTANCE.md and docs/SERVICE_INSTALLATION.md. Use the new managed Linux lifecycle tooling, SQLite, private retained state and an unused loopback port. Preserve the existing AI services and all unrelated data; do not change firewalls/proxies or expose public HTTP. Check health, service identity, listener and logs; perform one data-preserving uninstall/reinstall while stopped and confirm state/configuration continuity. Leave Mossward running locally for Uriah's first-time admin/MFA setup; do not choose his credentials or disable authentication. Setup-required readiness HTTP 503 is expected before user initialization. Authenticated scan and backup/update acceptance remain pending until initialization; scans are localhost-only and no other PC is authorized. Do not run disposable worker service tests on this shared host. Report actual sanitized check outcomes and pending user actions in the mailbox; retain private evidence locally, never publish secrets, raw logs, addresses or host paths. Reject conflicting existing Mossward resources and ask rather than overwrite. Clear wake metadata on acceptance per mailbox protocol. User authorization covers this installation and its scoped lifecycle checks, not unrelated product changes or publication.

Uriah requests more information about the failed installation job for request ubuntu-lab-install-20261010-240ea3c, digest 9ed50db2e8b02976763fa92c457d9da04c39ef6cb1aa798e4d018ff65d13ffe3, job 20261010T143053Z-f0f9ac5c. Read the existing private tracker receipts and logs; perform only safe read-only diagnostics needed to identify the failed step, exit status, sanitized error cause, whether this is a product defect or environment/test issue, and whether any Mossward service/files were installed or left running. Report the state of existing AI services, the recommended next action, and any questions requiring Uriah's input. Reconcile and publish an evidence-backed terminal result for the original request if supported by its receipts, and a separate diagnosis result for this new request. Do not rerun the failed job, retry installation, change product code, delete files, alter services, or access another PC under this diagnostic request. Preserve existing requests/results; publish only sanitized summaries and check outcomes, never raw logs, credentials, host paths or addresses. Clear wake metadata on acceptance according to mailbox protocol.

Uriah authorizes a NEW installation attempt after the completed diagnosis of ubuntu-lab-install-20261010-240ea3c. Preserve the original failed receipt and outcomes; do not relaunch its job or reuse its identity. Before launching this attempt, prepare a uniquely named reviewed orchestration script, syntax-check it with its actual shell, record its SHA-256 and preserve its exact bytes privately. Execute that immutable copy; never edit, replace or truncate any running script. Record the new request/digest/job linkage before execution and publish the actual outcome, including failures. Use this exact pinned product revision and follow docs/LINUX_LAB_ACCEPTANCE.md and docs/SERVICE_INSTALLATION.md. Run required verification, or document reuse of verified artifacts only if exact revision and artifact integrity are established. Recheck that no conflicting Mossward resources exist. Install using managed Linux tooling, SQLite and an unused loopback port; preserve unrelated AI services, data, firewalls and proxies. Verify low-privilege identity, local listener, health and logs, then one data-preserving uninstall/reinstall with stopped-state continuity checks. Leave the service running locally for Uriah's first-time admin/MFA setup; do not invent credentials or bypass authentication. Interpret readiness according to pinned code: local mode may return HTTP 200 with setup_required; hosted modes return HTTP 503 before setup. Authenticated scans and initialized backup/update checks remain pending until user setup. Scans are restricted to localhost, with no other-PC access or public exposure authorized. Do not run disposable worker service rehearsals on this shared host. Stop and ask on resource conflicts or uncertain failures; do not automatically retry again. Publish sanitized findings and user questions only, with no secrets, raw logs, addresses or private host paths. Clear wake metadata on acceptance under mailbox protocol.

Uriah requests the final reviewed report for completed installation retry ubuntu-lab-install-retry-20261010-002, digest 4ea67265ccb4757f0e3986dcb6bbff74c514a7f4edc8b6d40ddd461b5057cbd1, tracked job 20261010T145540Z-87e922c3. Its lifecycle acknowledgement says succeeded but results still say running. Review existing immutable execution evidence and receipts, plus safe read-only checks if needed. Reconcile the retry's actual terminal result and publish its build/test outcomes, whether Mossward is installed and currently running, service identity and loopback-only exposure, retained-state uninstall/reinstall results, existing AI-service health, failures or caveats, and pending user setup/actions. Do not infer all acceptance checks passed solely from tracker exit success. Publish a separate outcome for this reporting request. Request user admin/MFA initialization where needed; do not create credentials. Do not reinstall, rerun the installation job, update binaries, restart/change services, delete files, change product code or access another PC under this report-only request. Preserve prior request identities and evidence. Only sanitized summaries/check outcomes belong in this public mailbox; keep host addresses, private paths, secrets, raw logs and connection details private. Clear wake metadata on acceptance per mailbox protocol.

Uriah explicitly authorizes making the installed Mossward web interface accessible from his local network on this headless Linux server and requests discovery of its actual ports. First inspect the current service configuration, application listeners, any dedicated agent/worker listener, existing proxy and firewall read-only; report the current port numbers and transport modes. This request supersedes the prior loopback-only exposure restriction for the web interface only. Enable LAN access only through certificate-verified HTTPS using Mossward's existing TLS mode or an appropriate existing trusted HTTPS proxy, with matching public origin and WebAuthn RP/origin settings. Do not expose local-mode HTTP to the LAN, disable authentication/MFA, use insecure proxy trust, open databases or agent/worker listeners, create credentials, or request public Internet/router exposure. If a suitable certificate, user-approved hostname, trust provisioning, or unambiguous intended LAN interface/subnet is missing, report needs_input with the exact user choices needed before changing exposure; do not invent those choices or tell users to bypass certificate warnings. If prerequisites are already established, make only scoped reversible Mossward transport/proxy/firewall changes for the verified local network, preserve private config/state backups, restart Mossward as needed and verify service health, TLS validation and retained setup/identity. Do not alter unrelated AI services or existing certificates, broadly open firewall access, or contact/scan other PCs. Respect hosted setup_required readiness semantics before user initialization. Publish sanitized actual ports, checks, changes, pending questions and rollback guidance; provide actual host URL/address and private connection details through the user's private server channel, not this public mailbox. Use syntax-checked immutable scripts with recorded hashes for any tracked work; preserve previous outcomes, no automatic retry on failure. Clear wake metadata on acceptance per mailbox protocol.

Uriah supplies the requested LAN deployment choices and authorizes scoped activation: canonical hostname mossward.uriahmoss.com, HTTPS port 443 if unused otherwise 8443, and a locally generated temporary server certificate for now. Use the current home LAN interface/address established by local discovery; verify its actual subnet and bind specifically to that interface, not all interfaces. Generate a separate self-signed test web-server certificate with SAN for the canonical DNS name and confirmed current LAN IP, appropriate server-auth usage, private service-readable key permissions and bounded validity. Do not reuse endpoint PKI or commit certificates/keys. Provide public certificate fingerprint and explicit client trust and LAN DNS/hosts instructions through the private server channel; never advise bypassing certificate warnings or install trust on another PC without separate authorization. Configure supported direct TLS, exact public origin (including 8443 if selected), WebAuthn RP ID mossward.uriahmoss.com and matching HTTPS origin. Hostname is canonical for authentication/passkeys; report whether direct IP browsing is supported under pinned host/origin validation, without disabling those protections to make it work. Inspect both candidate ports and preserve existing AI/proxy listeners. Confirm the intended LAN interface/subnet before any narrowly scoped firewall change; do not create broad permits, modify router forwarding, enable public Internet exposure, expose databases/agent listeners, or contact another PC. Preserve private backups of affected configuration/state, use syntax-checked immutable scripts with hashes, and restart only Mossward as necessary. Honor pinned first-time setup controls: if secure hosted activation requires localhost administrator/MFA initialization first, prepare certificate/configuration but leave unsafe exposure disabled and report the exact tunnel/setup steps as needs_input. Do not create credentials, bypass authentication, weaken TLS or change product code. Verify certificate hostname/IP coverage, trusted TLS locally, service identity, LAN bind, preserved installation state, setup/readiness semantics and existing AI services. Report chosen port, actual changes, pending client trust/DNS/setup actions and rollback guidance with sanitized public outcomes; private host addresses, paths, keys and raw logs stay off this public mailbox. This supersedes only the earlier missing hostname/certificate/LAN prerequisites, not the security and other-PC restrictions. Clear wake metadata on acceptance.
